key_insight: The paper proposes a solved-volatility stochastic turbulence closure where displacement volatility is solved alongside velocity, using Itô–Hencky kinematics to enforce exact volume constraints and a consistent stochastic momentum balance.
engineering_relevance: This framework could improve turbulence models by making unresolved fluctuations dynamically coupled, physically constrained, and more suitable for finite-correlation and boundary-aware CFD closures.
method: One-channel Itô configuration map with local matrix-logarithm expansion.
Derives material/spatial Hencky increments, quadratic-variation drifts, and pathwise isochoricity.
Forms an index-one velocity–volatility–pressure DAE with source-consistent momentum and virtual-power stress separation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytic derivations and limiting-case consistency checks, but no numerical dataset or CFD validation in this paper.
watch_item: The closure is theory-complete but still lacks turbulent-statistics calibration and computational validation, so implementation may be sensitive to assumptions such as single-channel noise and boundary compatibility.
paper_title: Foundations of a solved-volatility stochastic turbulence closure: Itô--Hencky kinematics, source-consistent momentum and finite-correlation realisation
